record.paper_title: Challenges and open problems in computational prediction of protein complexes: the case of membrane complexes
record.original_question: How can computational methods extract the membrane protein subinteractome, meaning the set of interactions among membrane proteins, so that membrane protein complexes can be reconstructed from membrane-protein interaction data despite the scarcity of characterized membrane complexes with known protein-protein interactions?

evidence.quote: One major avenue is to understand membrane proteins and their complexes is to map the membrane protein ‘subinteractomes’, the set of interactions among membrane proteins.
The need now is to develop effective computational techniques to mine this membrane subinteractome data to reconstruct membrane complexes.
a) How to extract out the membrane ‘subinteractome’? • Very few membrane complexes characterised for PPIs.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open methodological challenge in computational biology: reliably extracting membrane protein subinteractomes and reconstructing membrane complexes from sparse PPI data. Subsequent literature on membrane interactome mapping (e.g., MYTH/split-ubiquitin screens, membrane-focused complex prediction methods) has expanded available data and clustering approaches, but no general computational solution overcomes the scarcity of characterized membrane complexes; the problem is generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Challenges and open problems in computational prediction of protein complexes
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies extracting the membrane subinteractome and reconstructing membrane complexes as an open challenge given few characterized membrane complexes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of extracting membrane subinteractomes for complex reconstruction is identified as an unresolved computational challenge.

status_evidence.title: Mapping the human membrane protein interactome (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews indicate that membrane PPI data remain sparse and underrepresented in standard interactomes, and dedicated computational methods are still being developed.
status_evidence.claim: Sparse coverage of membrane PPIs continues to limit complex reconstruction, supporting that the methodological problem remains open.
